nodes.title: Dualizing Deligne pairing
nodes.statement: For g≥2 and f:C→M̄_g over Z, construct P_g=⟨ω_f,ω_f⟩ as a line object on M̄_g. Precisely, P_g is a cartesian assignment to each T-valued stable curve of the GPAIR line ⟨ω_C/T,ω_C/T⟩ in the core of InvertibleSheaf T, together with base-change isomorphisms and their cocycle. Equivalently it is a 1-morphism M̄_g→BG_m, using the existing line-stack equivalence. Its tensor operations and isomorphisms occur in this Picard groupoid, not in its set of isomorphism classes.
hypotheses: g≥2; universal unpointed stable curve; untwisted relative dualizing sheaf.
GDET/GPAIR and the arbitrary-base nodal-dualizing extension in gap NODAL-BC are supplied.
proofSteps: On a scheme chart use the parent stable-curve dualizing line, local projectivity of a stable curve and the integral GPAIR construction.
Its canonical base-change comparisons, and the dualizing base-change maps, give descent along the chart groupoid.
Apply SF.1 line-stack equivalence and effective descent to obtain a line on the stack; verify identity, composition and 2-isomorphism invariance.

sources.match: Uses the universal relative-dualizing pairing and its classifying pullback.
Supplies the actual line-valued chart construction and coherent arbitrary base change, permitting effective descent.

acceptance: A chartwise line plus class equality is insufficient: its actual comparison morphisms satisfy the groupoid cocycle.
Specialization to a nodal F_p-valued stable curve is admitted.
The universal line is independent, up to the specified coherent isomorphism, of a choice of chart.

uses.how: Provides the line on the right-hand side, integrally over Z.
Identifies classifying pullback with the family pairing, including singular and nonreduced bases.

nodes.title: Hodge determinant and derived direct image
nodes.statement: For a proper stable family f:C→S of connected arithmetic genus g, let E=f_*ω and λ=det E. There are natural underlying-line isomorphisms d_f(ω)≅λ and d_f(O_C)≅λ, coherent with arbitrary base change. In graded lines their integer degrees are respectively g−1 and 1−g; these grades are not silently identified with the ordinary rank-g determinant grading.
hypotheses: S a scheme chart of the stable stack, including arbitrary base via NODAL-BC.
Relative trace R¹f_*ω≅O_S and Serre duality R¹f_*O≅E∨, with f_*O≅O_S.
proofSteps: Use the parent connected-nodal cohomology and duality contracts to identify the two cohomology sheaves in degrees zero and one.
Compute the alternating determinant, retaining the trace trivialization and canonical double-dual comparison.
Transport the identifications along derived base change; check the equality of grades and descent separately from the underlying line.

sources.match: Defines the Hodge line by the derived determinant and compares the O and dualizing determinants using curve duality.
Uses the determinant of the derived direct image for the Hodge and pluricanonical lines.
Specifies the graded determinant-of-cohomology convention used in the comparison.

acceptance: For g=0 on a stable pointed genus-zero family, both underlying lines are trivial but the two derived grades are −1 and +1.
For a smooth genus-one family, both derived grades are zero while E has rank one.
R¹f_*ω cannot be omitted from the determinant formula.

nodes.title: Noether defect line
nodes.statement: For g≥2 define the line N_g=λ_g^{⊗12}⊗P_g∨⊗O(−Δ) as an object of the line Picard groupoid on M̄_g/Z, where P_g is the actual universal dualizing pairing and O(−Δ)=O(Δ)∨. Its class vanishes exactly when a Noether isomorphism λ_g^{⊗12}≅P_g⊗O(Δ) exists. This criterion concerns existence; the set of choices is a torsor under global units.
hypotheses: g≥2; use the reduced local-node boundary convention of the imported boundary-divisor node.
All tensor powers, duals, evaluation and cancellation maps live in the stack Picard groupoid supplied by SF.1/SF.3.
proofSteps: Apply tensor, dual and powers to the imported Hodge and boundary lines and the constructed P_g.
Tensor cancellation identifies trivializations of N_g with Noether comparison isomorphisms.
The Picard-groupoid unit automorphisms identify the ratio of two trivializations with a global unit.

sources.match: The three lines and the universal-choice convention yield this obstruction line by tensor cancellation.
Separates the rational computation, torsion-freeness step and integral descent; the defect packages precisely those steps.

acceptance: The boundary occurs with a negative sign in N_g and a positive sign on the right of the Noether isomorphism.
A vanishing rational Chern class alone does not construct a trivialization.
Two comparisons are compared as maps of line objects before passing to classes.

uses.how: Turns rational GRR plus the pairing Chern comparison into a torsion class.
The Picard injection and complex torsion-freeness kill this integral obstruction line.

api.name: noetherDefect_pullback
api.statement: Pull back N_g with its tensor and dual comparisons along any classifying map; for arbitrary families the boundary term means the pullback line.

api.name: noetherDefect_trivialization
api.statement: Trivializations N_g≅O correspond to isomorphisms λ_g^12≅P_g⊗O(Δ), with inverse given by tensor cancellation.

api.name: noetherDefect_class
api.statement: Its Picard class is 12[λ_g]−[P_g]−[O(Δ)]; on an actual scheme chart equality of line classes is the pinned nonempty-isomorphism criterion.

api.name: noetherDefect_ratio
api.statement: Given two trivializations, a unique unit takes one to the other; class equality contains no preferred choice.

tests.name: three-trivial-lines
tests.statement: If λ, P and O(Δ) are equipped with trivializations on a test scheme, the induced N is trivial; changing a trivialization changes the map, not its class.

tests.name: boundary-sign
tests.statement: For a trait with one split node xy=π^m, the canonical rational section of the boundary factor O(−Δ) in N has order −m; the section of O(Δ) on the Noether right-hand side has order +m. This does not assign an order to an unspecified rational section of the whole defect line.

tests.name: rational-torsion
tests.statement: For a nontrivial torsion line, vanishing in Pic⊗Q does not give an integral trivialization; the proof must still use complex torsion-freeness.

tests.name: nonuniversal-unit
tests.statement: On a Q-scheme, multiplying a comparison by 2 produces another comparison. It need not be the pullback of a universal choice differing by ±1.

nodes.title: Chern class of the dualizing pairing
nodes.statement: On M̄_g/C, g≥2, the universal pairing satisfies c₁(P_g)=f_*(c₁(ω_f)²) in CH¹(M̄_g/C;Q). The scheme-level integral input is the degree-one graded-K comparison for Deligne pairings on divisorial bases. Its passage to rational Chow and then to the moduli stack must use named comparison/descent maps, and is not an integral identification of arbitrary stack Chow and Picard groups.
hypotheses: Use SF.5 stack Chow with rational coefficients and its actual first-Chern/proper-pushforward operations.
Supply gap CHOW-PIC: pairing Chern comparison and codimension-one Picard comparison for this smooth DM stack, including stabilizers.
proofSteps: On a suitable divisorial scheme chart apply Eriksson–Freixas Corollary 6.9 to the two line arguments.
Use the rational Chern-character comparison to convert its graded-K identity to Chow.

Use a smooth equivariant Hilbert presentation of the moduli stack and compatible mixed quotients (Edidin–Graham, Propositions 14–19), so that the chart computation is an equivariant identity and not merely an identity after forgetting equivariance. Theorem 3.1 of their Riemann–Roch paper supplies the compatible proper pushforward. Supply the comparison to the chosen SF.5 stack-Chow carrier in CHOW-PIC; pullback to a plain atlas alone is not an injection on Picard groups.

sources.match: Identifies the Deligne-pairing Chern class with the direct image in graded K-theory under the divisorial-base hypothesis. The projection-formula display in the Proposition 6.8 proof omits a gamma operation on its left side (confirmed E18); the intended graded K-group statement and Corollary 6.9 are unchanged.
Supplies the moduli rational computation, including the local singularity correction; a formal stack Chow comparison is still required.

sources.locator: Theorem 1, pp. 7–8; Corollary 1, p. 9; Propositions 14–19, pp. 28–29
sources.match: Gives the equivariant Chern/Picard comparison, its quotient-stack interpretation and rational intersection-product compatibility.
Supplies proper equivariant pushforward and the smooth/qualified-lci Riemann–Roch compatibilities needed in a quotient presentation, with rational coefficients.

acceptance: State the divisorial-scheme hypothesis before using Corollary 6.9.
The smooth-scheme GRR signature is not advertised as arbitrary singular or stack GRR.
The sign in the pairing term is positive.

nodes.title: Rational Noether computation gives a torsion defect
nodes.statement: For g≥2 the class [N_g/C] is torsion in Pic(M̄_g/C). Equivalently, some positive tensor power of N_g/C is trivial. This is the precise intermediate conclusion of rational Noether: 12c₁λ=f_*(c₁ω²)+[Δ] together with the pairing Chern comparison and the rational codimension-one Picard–Chow comparison.
hypotheses: The imported rational-noether identity is over C and has coefficient one on every reduced universal node branch.
CHOW-PIC supplies an injective Pic⊗Q→CH¹⊗Q comparison for the actual stack; N_g is a genuine line, not a rational formal symbol.
proofSteps: Compute c₁(N_g/C) from its three factors and cancel using rational Noether and pairing-chern-on-moduli.
Transport the vanishing to Pic⊗Q through the specified codimension-one comparison.
Use that the kernel of an abelian group’s map to its rationalization is its torsion subgroup; do not infer [N]=0 integrally yet.

sources.match: First obtains the line relation rationally and then needs a separate torsion-freeness theorem to make it integral.
States the integral endpoint, for which this node supplies only the rational/torsion intermediate step.
Identifies equivariant Picard and codimension-one Chow for a smooth quotient presentation; rationalization detects exactly the torsion ambiguity.

acceptance: The conclusion includes an existential positive exponent, not a canonical trivialization or an asserted exponent 12.
A torsion character line on Bμ_r over C demonstrates why a rational class identity does not by itself imply an integral one.

nodes.title: Boundary twists kill torsion-line monodromy
nodes.statement: Let g≥2 and L be an r-torsion line on M̄_g/C with a chosen L^r≅O and r≥1. The associated μ_r-torsor on the stack has trivial monodromy on M_g/C: after analytification and pullback to Teichmüller space, its character Mod_g→μ_r is trivial. Indeed extension over each transverse one-node smoothing kills the associated Dehn twist, and Dehn twists generate Mod_g. The torsor is then trivial over the normal compactified stack, so L is trivial. Quotient stacks and their inertia are retained throughout; a coarse-space argument is insufficient, including in genus two.
hypotheses: Use algebraic finite étale μ_r-torsors over C, where r is invertible; do not use the same étale argument in characteristic dividing r.

TOPOLOGY supplies the analytic stack quotient [T_g/Mod_g], simple connectedness of T_g, mapping-class generation, nodal monodromy and cover comparison, including algebraic recovery on the proper DM stack.
proofSteps: Construct Spec(⊕_{i=0}^{r−1}L^i), with multiplication from L^r≅O, using the existing torsor/relative-Spec machinery.

Pull the analytic torsor to the contractible Teichmüller space. Descent along the action groupoid T_g×Mod_g gives a character of the full mapping-class group. The nerve has action face maps: it is not the product simplicial object with constant T_g; its realization is a homotopy quotient with contractible fibre over BMod_g (sourceIssues E16–E17).
A transverse smoothing disk has trivial étale/topological cover when filled in, so the loop around its puncture acts trivially; its mapping-class monodromy is the corresponding Dehn twist.

Use Luo’s generation theorem to kill the character. Extend the analytic cover splitting from the dense smooth locus across the normal compactified stack by normalization, retaining inertia; the disk argument is applied in stack charts. Hall Theorem 1 with proper DM source M̄_g/C and target Bμ_r algebraizes the trivialization and its inverse. Equivalently apply separated GAGA to the line isomorphism on the proper stack.

sources.locator: Lemma 5.14, statement p. 102 and proof pp. 103–105
sources.match: Uses the Teichmüller-space cover, mapping-class characters and boundary Dehn twists to eliminate torsion; the cited analytic inputs require separate supplier contracts.

sources.locator: Theorem 2.5 and Proposition 2.6, p. 11; §2.3, pp. 17–19, with corrections E16–E17 below
sources.match: Supplies Teichmüller representability and contractibility. Use the action groupoid and homotopy quotient, retaining stabilizers; the displayed product-of-simplicial-spaces proof is corrected in sourceIssues.
Presents the orientation-preserving mapping class group of a compact oriented surface by all Dehn twists, hence gives generation for the closed genus-g surface.

sources.locator: Theorem 1, p. 1; Theorem A.1 and Corollary A.3, p. 17
sources.match: For a proper DM source, analytification recovers morphisms to the DM target Bμ_r and their isomorphisms. Separated GAGA also recovers coherent line isomorphisms on the proper compactification.

acceptance: Include separating as well as nonseparating nodal monodromy, and do not suppress inertia by replacing the stack with its coarse space.
For r=1 the torsor is trivial. For arbitrary r over C it is étale; this reasoning does not assert the same in characteristic p dividing r.
Triviality on the dense open is extended by normality, not by an unproved claim that restriction of arbitrary line bundles is injective.

nodes.title: A complex trivialization descends to the rational fibre
nodes.statement: Let X=M̄_g/Z, g≥2, and L a line on X. If L_C is trivial, then L_Q is trivial. More precisely H⁰(X_Q,L_Q)⊗_Q C≅H⁰(X_C,L_C) is one-dimensional, because Γ(X_C,O)=C. Choose a nonzero rational section in this space; after base change it is a nonzero constant multiple of a trivialization and hence nowhere vanishing. Faithful flatness then makes its evaluation O_XQ→L_Q an isomorphism.
hypotheses: Proper stable-moduli stack over Z, and the geometrically connected/irreducible fibre statements imported from MC.1/MC.4.
DESCENT supplies H⁰ flat field-extension base change on the proper DM stack and descent of the evaluation isomorphism.
No claim is made that a line trivial after every arbitrary field extension descends without these H⁰ hypotheses.
proofSteps: Use flat cohomology base change for Q→C, without asserting the chosen complex section itself has rational coefficients.
The right-hand H⁰ has dimension one since the line is trivial and the proper connected complex stack has only constant functions.
A nonzero rational vector becomes a nonzero scalar multiple of a complex trivialization. Descend invertibility of its evaluation map by faithful flatness.

sources.match: Uses invariant global sections and flat base change to pass from a complex trivial line to a rational section, before the vertical-divisor argument.

acceptance: One-dimensionality is proved before selecting the rational section.
The evaluation map, rather than only its space of sections, descends as an isomorphism.
The argument respects stabilizer actions and thus applies to the stack line, not only its atlas restriction.

nodes.title: Vertical divisors on the integral stable stack
nodes.statement: For X=M̄_g/Z, g≥2, every Cartier divisor whose support is vertical is a finite sum D=Σ_p n_p X_Fp of whole prime fibres, with integral n_p. Since X/Z is smooth with geometrically irreducible fibres, each X_Fp is reduced, irreducible and Cartier of multiplicity one. Consequently D=div_X(∏_p p^{n_p}). In particular, for any line L on X, a trivialization of L|X_Q extends after multiplication by a rational number to a nowhere-vanishing section on X.
hypotheses: X is the smooth integral noetherian stable DM stack with geometrically irreducible fibres.
DIVISORS supplies Cartier/Weil comparison, divisors of rational sections and the codimension-one criterion on a smooth DM stack, extending the scheme-only SF.3 excision result.
proofSteps: A codimension-one irreducible vertical support lies over a unique prime and equals that whole irreducible fibre; use smoothness and dimension to exclude a proper codimension-one subvariety of the fibre.
Smoothness makes each prime fibre reduced, and flatness makes p a nonzerodivisor, with divisor exactly that fibre.
A Cartier divisor has finitely many such components on the quasi-compact stack. Compare with the principal divisor of the rational number ∏p^{n_p}.
For a line rationally trivialized on X_Q, subtract this principal divisor from the divisor of its rational section; regularity/codimension-one comparison then makes it a global trivialization.

sources.locator: Integral descent after Lemma 5.14, printed pp. 102–103
sources.match: Removes vertical zeros or poles by whole-prime-fibre principal divisors, proving the needed integral restriction injectivity.

acceptance: Negative coefficients are allowed; the correcting scalar belongs to Q×, not necessarily Z.
Multiplicity one uses smoothness; the same formula without multiplicities is false for a nonreduced prime fibre.
The scheme excision node does not already prove this stack statement.

nodes.title: Noether isomorphism under arbitrary classifying pullback
nodes.statement: Choose one universal integral isomorphism e:λ_g^12≅P_g⊗O(Δ), g≥2. For every stable genus-g family C→S classified by c:S→M̄_g, pullback and the Hodge/pairing comparisons give an actual line isomorphism (det f_*ω)^12≅⟨ω,ω⟩⊗c*O(Δ), coherent under arbitrary base change and isomorphisms of families. If S is integral noetherian and the family is generically smooth, c*O(Δ)=O(Δ_S) with its pulled-back effective-Cartier section. For a family lying in the boundary, c*O(Δ) still exists but its pulled-back section can be zero and need not cut out an effective Cartier divisor. Any two universal choices differ by ±1, whose images may coincide over characteristic two. Arbitrary family isomorphisms can instead differ by any unit on S.
hypotheses: All stable-family Hodge and dualizing base-change comparisons have been extended to arbitrary bases as specified in NODAL-BC.
The imported integral-noether and universal-units theorems give a universal choice and its universal ambiguity.
An effective-Cartier family boundary is asserted only under the stated integral/noetherian/generically-smooth hypotheses.
proofSteps: Apply the stack Picard pullback functor to e; identify its left side using Hodge base change and AV determinant pullback.
Identify the pairing by universal-dualizing-pairing and keep the boundary as a line with its pulled-back section.
Use nonvanishing of the generic smoothing parameters only when identifying the pulled-back section with a Cartier divisor.
Transport the unique ratio unit of two universal comparisons through the same pullback functor; Γ(M̄_g/Z,O×)=Z× supplies ±1.

sources.match: States the classifying-pullback comparison and its universal-choice interpretation for generically smooth integral Noetherian families; arbitrary-base line pullback here follows from the explicit stack line and base-change contracts.
Provides the nonflat and non-Noetherian pairing base-change input for the stated extension.

acceptance: For a stable nodal curve over a field, the boundary line pulls back while its boundary section is zero; do not call that zero locus an effective Cartier divisor.
For xy=π^m on a trait, the pulled-back boundary section has order m, not one.
On an F₂-scheme the two universal signs have identical images. On a Q-scheme, multiplying a family comparison by 2 shows why arbitrary comparisons are not exhausted by the universal choices.

sourceIssues.locator: arXiv:math/0404387v1, §2.3, p. 18, paragraph following the two local-isomorphism projections
sourceIssues.printed: The text invokes rigidity of the marked data and calls the arrow-to-object-pair map an immersion.
sourceIssues.correction: Retain stabilizer arrows after forgetting markings. The action groupoid for G=1 is not a monomorphism over T_g×T_g, but its arrow map is locally a graph because its source projection is a local isomorphism. This is compatible with analytic immersion in the local differential sense.
sourceIssues.reason: At a genus-two point the identity and hyperelliptic involution give two arrows over (x,x). This disproves global monomorphism, not local analytic immersion. In a source chart the arrow map is a holomorphic graph, hence an immersion in the differential sense. The alleged source error depends on reading immersion as a locally closed embedding and is not established by this example.

sourceIssues.locator: arXiv:math/0404387v1, §2.3, p. 18, fibre formula near the bottom
sourceIssues.printed: The fibre over fixed x of the arrow-space projection is identified with T_g^G×Γ_g,G.
sourceIssues.correction: The entire arrow space has that product form in the intended quotient presentation. A fixed source fibre is the discrete group Γ_g,G, with its target determined by the action; for G=1 this is Mod_g.
sourceIssues.reason: The projection is already stated to be a local isomorphism, hence its point fibres are discrete. With G=1 and g≥2, T_g has positive dimension 3g−3, so its product with Mod_g cannot be such a fibre.

review.reason: The printed fixed-source fibre cannot contain the positive-dimensional Teichmüller factor when the projection is a local isomorphism. The G=1, g=2 specialization already proves the dimensional contradiction; the full arrow space and a source fibre have been confused.

sourceIssues.locator: arXiv:math/0404387v1, Proposition 2.14 proof, p. 19, product-simplicial-object identification
sourceIssues.printed: The degreewise products in the action-groupoid nerve are treated as a product simplicial object T_g^G×BΓ_g,G and used to assert a product realization.
sourceIssues.correction: Use the action nerve, whose realization is EΓ_g,G×_Γ_g,G T_g^G. Its projection to BΓ_g,G has contractible fibre T_g^G and yields the required homotopy equivalence. The constant-product simplicial identification is not justified.
sourceIssues.reason: Already for G=1 and an element γ moving x, the two degree-one face maps of the action arrow (x,γ) are x and γx. In the constant-T_g product with BMod_g both faces keep the same T_g coordinate. The degreewise product bijections therefore do not respect the simplicial maps. This repairs the proof without rejecting the proposition’s homotopy-equivalence conclusion.

review.reason: For an action moving x the two arrow faces land at different points, whereas the proposed constant-space product keeps x fixed. Thus the degreewise product is not a simplicial identification. The Borel construction gives the required homotopy equivalence without this identification.

sourceIssues.locator: Published J. Éc. polytech. Math. 11 (2024), Proposition 6.8 proof, printed p. 317, unnumbered projection-formula display after the complete-flag construction
sourceIssues.printed: The left side of the projection-formula display uses the factor [E]−r, whereas the right side retains its k₀-th gamma operation.
sourceIssues.correction: Retain γ^{k₀}([E]−r) on the left as well as on the right. The other factors and the complete-flag pushforward remain as in the intended argument.
sourceIssues.reason: Take f:P¹_k→Spec(k), E=O(1), r=1, k₀=3 and no other gamma factors. The complete-flag map is the identity and its extra product is 1. The printed left side has Euler characteristic χ(O(1))−χ(O)=1. On the right γ³([O(1)]−1)=0 because the gamma series for a line minus 1 has only its linear term. Restoring the gamma operation makes both sides zero and restores the filtration degree needed for n=1.

proposedSupplierContracts.status: Unassigned extension; a recorded gap, not an existing supplier stage.
proposedSupplierContracts.need: For schemes, realize the commutative-ring virtual determinant in graded invertible sheaves, descend it from finite-projective complexes to perfect complexes and glue. For proper flat finitely presented f, perfect E has perfect Rf_*E and λ_f(E)=det Rf_*E commutes with arbitrary derived base change. Locally λ_f(E) has line ⊗_i(det P^i)^{(−1)^i} and grade Σ_i(−1)^i rank(P^i) for a finite-projective model of Rf_*E. Quasi-isomorphisms and acyclic models have the specified canonical comparisons; exact-sequence and shift comparisons retain Koszul signs. This is not the assertion that every distinguished triangle has a functorial arbitrary-triangle determinant isomorphism.

sources.locator: §1, pp. 20–21; Lemma 2, p. 28; bounded-complex formula, pp. 30–32

api.name: detPerfect_affine
api.statement: On an affine and a degree-zero finite projective module, agree with AV-L0C exterior determinant, with grade equal to its rank.

api.name: detPerfect_acyclic
api.statement: An acyclic perfect complex has the canonical determinant trivialization, compatible with quasi-isomorphisms.

api.name: detPerfect_shortExact
api.statement: A short exact sequence of perfect complex models gives a natural additivity isomorphism with the Knudsen–Mumford coherence laws.

api.name: detPerfect_shift
api.statement: Shifting by one inverts the graded line; the integer grade changes sign.

api.name: detCohomology_baseChange
api.statement: For every S′→S, derived base change identifies pullback of λ_f(E) with λ_f′(Lh*E), with identity and composition cocycles.

api.name: detCohomology_duality
api.statement: Use actual curve Serre duality to compare det Rf_*O and det Rf_*ω with the ordinary Hodge determinant; do not identify their integer grades.

tests.name: degree-zero-rank-two
tests.statement: For R² in degree zero the line is ∧²R² and the grade is 2; exchanging the two standard basis vectors acts by −1.

tests.name: identity-complex
tests.statement: For [R --id→ R] in degrees 0,1 the grade is 0 and the canonical acyclic determinant is R.

tests.name: shifted-line
tests.statement: For R concentrated in degree 1 the determinant line is R∨ and its grade is −1, rather than +1.

tests.name: nonflat-specialization
tests.statement: The required base-change map exists for Spec(F_p)→Spec(Z); requiring this map to be flat fails the contract.

tests.name: projective-line
tests.statement: For P¹_R→Spec(R), λ(O(1)) is det(R²) of grade 2, while λ(O(−2)) has grade −1; these are not both H⁰ determinants.

proposedSupplierContracts.status: Unassigned extension; a recorded gap, not an existing supplier stage.
proposedSupplierContracts.need: For f:X→S locally projective, faithfully flat, finitely presented and of pure relative dimension one, construct the integral Deligne pairing on actual line bundles, with arbitrary base change. Put d(A)=underlying line of λ_f(A). In the fixed order, ⟨L,M⟩=d(L⊗M)⊗d(O_X)⊗d(L)∨⊗d(M)∨. The determinant calculation is made in graded lines before passing to its grade-zero line. Coherent bilinearity, permutation, norm and divisor comparisons are data to prove, not consequences of an equality in K₀ or Pic⊗Q. No smoothness or Noetherian assumption is imposed.

sources.match: Gives the rank-zero determinant expression and the coherent bilinear comparison for proper flat curves, beyond the smooth discussion in §6.
Supplies the locally projective arbitrary-base version and the sign, scalar and relative-divisor laws.

api.name: delignePairing_detComparison
api.statement: Use exactly the four-term determinant expression above; its Euler-characteristic grade is zero by curve Riemann–Roch.

api.name: delignePairing_bilinear
api.statement: Tensor-product additivity in both arguments, coherent with unit, associativity, interchange and permutations.

api.name: delignePairing_baseChange
api.statement: Pullback identifies the pairing with the pairing on the cartesian family for every base morphism; identity and composition comparisons satisfy descent.

api.name: delignePairing_relativeDivisor
api.statement: For a relative effective Cartier divisor D finite flat over S, identify ⟨O(D),M⟩ with N_D/S(M|D). If D is empty on an open-and-closed component, the value there is the trivial line.

api.name: delignePairing_scalar
api.statement: Multiplication by u on L acts on the pairing by u^{deg(M)} on each rank/degree component.

api.name: delignePairing_selfSymmetry
api.statement: The canonical interchange on ⟨L,L⟩ is multiplication by (−1)^{deg(L)}. It is not always the identity.

api.name: delignePairing_firstChern
api.statement: On the divisorial-scheme range of Corollary 6.9 identify the pairing class with the degree-two Chern pushforward in the graded K-group; the Chow and stack extensions are separate named needs.

tests.name: trivial-argument
tests.statement: ⟨O_X,M⟩ has the bilinear unit trivialization; omitting the d(O_X) term breaks this normalization.

tests.name: section-divisor
tests.statement: For a section s in the smooth locus, ⟨O(s),M⟩≅s*M by the degree-one norm; no inverse appears.

tests.name: odd-self-symmetry
tests.statement: For P¹_k and L=O(1), the canonical self-interchange is −1 when char(k)≠2, even though the pairing line is one-dimensional.

tests.name: dualizing-even-degree
tests.statement: For a connected stable genus-g fibre, deg(ω)=2g−2 is even, so self-interchange of ⟨ω,ω⟩ is +1.

tests.name: base-line-degree
tests.statement: For L=f*A, identify ⟨f*A,M⟩ with A^{deg(M)}. For M=O(1) on P¹ this is A, not A∨.

tests.name: nodal-nonflat-base-change
tests.statement: For a stable nodal family over Z and its F_p fibre, the integral pairing specializes; a smooth-family-only or flat-base-change-only definition fails.

tests.name: finite-flat-norm
tests.statement: For a relative divisor of degree two, multiplication by u on M acts by u² on its norm pairing, not by u.

importedTargets.provides: The rank-g Hodge bundle on every stable pointed stack, with untwisted ω and arbitrary base change.
The ordinary determinant line; replace the legacy SF.5 determinant citation by AV-L0B/L0C plus stack descent.
Coherent forgetting/stabilization comparison, only where the target stable moduli problem exists.
Ordered direct-sum and determinant comparison with exchange sign (−1)^{g₁g₂}.
Ordered-residue exact sequence; branch exchange negates the quotient residue.
Universal effective Cartier boundary and its conditional effective-Cartier family pullback.
Complex rational GRR identity; it remains a rational Chow computation.
No torsion in the complex compactified stack Picard group.
Restriction from Z to C is injective on Picard groups.
The integral universal line-isomorphism existence theorem.
Global functions Z and units ±1 on the integral universal stack.
Pullbacks of universal choices; not a classification of all family isomorphisms.
Residue-weighted sum of node thicknesses at codimension-one traits.

api.name: hodge_rank
api.statement: E=f_*ω is locally free of constant rank g.

api.name: hodge_baseChange
api.statement: For every base change h, h*E≅E′, with the identity/composition cocycle.

api.name: hodge_untwisted
api.statement: Use ω, not ω(sum of markings); the usual Serre trace comparison is retained.

tests.name: genus-zero-three-marks
tests.statement: On M̄_0,3 the Hodge bundle is zero; f_*ω(sum marks) has rank two and is the wrong definition.

tests.name: genus-one
tests.statement: On M̄_1,1 the Hodge bundle has rank one, not the number of markings.

tests.name: separating-two-elliptic
tests.statement: A genus-two fibre made from two elliptic components has Hodge space the direct sum of their one-dimensional spaces.

api.name: hodgeDet_rankZero
api.statement: The determinant of the zero bundle is the trivial line.

api.name: hodgeDet_baseChange
api.statement: Use AV-L0C coherent pullback and descend this comparison to the stack.

api.name: hodgeDet_orderedSum
api.statement: Concatenated wedge bases determine the direct-sum determinant comparison; exchanging blocks changes it by (−1)^{g₁g₂}.

tests.name: genus-zero-line
tests.statement: Although E has rank zero, λ has rank one and is canonically trivial.

tests.name: one-plus-one-swap
tests.statement: Swapping two genus-one Hodge blocks acts by −1 before specializing to characteristic two.

tests.name: ordered-residue
tests.statement: For nonseparating clutching, the two residue orderings differ by −1 on the quotient line, even when the underlying λ line is isomorphic in both descriptions.

api.name: boundary_line_section
api.statement: Use (O(Δ),s_Δ) on the stack; locally s_Δ is the product of the node smoothing parameters.

api.name: boundary_pullback
api.statement: The line and section pull back along every map; Cartier-divisor pullback requires the pulled-back section to be regular.

api.name: boundary_trait
api.statement: On a normal generically smooth trait the order is the residue-degree-weighted sum of smoothing thicknesses.

tests.name: one-thick-node
tests.statement: For xy=π³, the order is 3.

tests.name: two-nodes
tests.statement: For split nodes of thicknesses 2 and 5, the total order is 7.

tests.name: nonsplit-node
tests.statement: A closed node of residue degree d and thickness m contributes d·m before splitting.

tests.name: wholly-boundary
tests.statement: A nodal stable curve over a field has pulled-back section zero; its line still exists but the zero subscheme is not an effective Cartier divisor.

api.name: semiCanonical_fromUniversal
api.statement: Fix a universal line comparison; its pullback with the stated Hodge/pairing comparisons is a semi-canonical family comparison.

api.name: semiCanonical_ratio
api.statement: Two universal choices differ by a unique element of Z×={±1}; their family pullbacks differ by its image in Γ(S,O_S)×.

api.name: semiCanonical_baseChange
api.statement: The chosen comparisons commute with arbitrary classifying pullback, with the Cartier-boundary interpretation restricted to generically smooth integral Noetherian bases.

tests.name: integer-units
tests.statement: On the universal integral stack the two comparison choices differ by +1 or −1, with no other unit available.

tests.name: characteristic-two
tests.statement: After pullback to a characteristic-two scheme the two signs coincide, so the family set of induced choices need not have two distinct elements.

tests.name: extra-family-unit
tests.statement: On a Q-scheme, multiplying any comparison by 2 gives a valid family comparison whose ratio is not the image of a universal sign; the definition does not classify all family isomorphisms.
